description: Only the witness hook tells an engine that loses the chosen derivation's witness from a correct one. Under late-elision, a, with one elided T, beats b, with two. In the check, a restores T, and c and d each read the synthetic T as a bare terminal, so R has three readings and the check fails. An engine that loses a's restoration still finds c and d, and gives the same public result. The runner's witness hook fails it, since the forest no longer holds W(D) (engine §7.8, tests/README.md).
grammar:
%ambiguity-resolution late-elision elision-only
%elidable T
%rule text a | b | c | d
%rule a A [T]
%rule b A [T] [T]
%rule c A T
%rule d A T
